ai.description: *Hemidactylus triedrus* reaches 13 cm. It is pale yellow or olive with dark, white-spotted crossbands. Distinctive features include large, trihedral tubercles on the back and a vertically slit pupil.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hemidactylus triedrus* is best distinguished by the three rows of enlarged, trihedral tubercles on its back, which are notably larger than those of other Indian species.
ai.habitat: *Hemidactylus triedrus* inhabits dry deciduous forests, rocky outcrops, and scrublands across the Indian subcontinent, ranging from sea level up to approximately 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: *Hemidactylus triedrus* is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to actively hunt insects and small invertebrates while utilizing its adhesive toe pads to climb vertical walls.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus triedrus* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding occurs primarily during the monsoon season, from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemidactylus triedrus* is found across peninsular India, ranging from dry deciduous forests to rocky outcrops, typically from sea level up to 1,000 meters in elevation.
